title: Trailhead: mini-PRD + experiment notes
content:
Context:

Quick notepad for the Trailhead idea — a small, opinionated feature to help customers prototype lower-cost response tiers with minimal product changes. Mix of product intent, API sketch, acceptance criteria and experiment plan. This is a rough PRD-level sketch + parking lot of questions.

Problem we want to address:
- Many teams want to reduce per-token cost while preserving acceptable UX. They don't want a heavy engineering lift (new models, infra changes).
- Current knobs (model selection, quantization, batching) live in a few places (console, SDK flags) but customers struggle to evaluate trade-offs quickly and rollout safely.

Trailhead objective (one-sentence):
Provide a lightweight, safe path for app teams to route a small percent of traffic to lower-cost response options (approximation tiers) with built-in telemetry and automatic rollback triggers.

Key principles:
- Minimal client changes: a single per-request header or route config toggle to opt-in to Trailhead.
- Safe by default: small percent, circuit-breaker style rollback, canary + automatic fallout detection.
- Observable: per-trial telemetry surfaced in Redwood Console (latency, per-token cost, quality deltas on eval set).
- Fast iteration: enable toggles for trial cohorts without provisioning new infra.

Feature sketch:
1) Trailhead Route Configuration (Console / API)
   - route config: { trial_name, percent, fallback_policy, approximation_profile }
   - approximation_profile: preset (e.g., low-cost-quantized, short-context, small-model) or custom selection of model_variant + quantization + caching behavior.
2) Per-request opt-in
   - SDK/REST: add header X-Trailhead-Cohort: <trial_name> or route-level assignment in Console
3) Runtime routing rules
   - Smart sampling: accept requests for trial up to percent, otherwise pass-through to primary model
   - When approx variant fails (errors, OOM), fallback immediately to primary model
4) Safety & automatic rollback signals
   - SLOs to watch: error-rate, end-to-end latency (tail), token-efficiency delta, user-defined quality regression metric (via eval hook)
   - If N% worse on quality or error-rate > threshold for M minutes, auto-disable trial and send alert
5) Visuals in Console
   - Trial dashboard: cohort size, traffic %, cost delta (tokens * price), sample responses diff (random sampling), and eval-set regression charts

User stories:
- As an engineering lead, I want to try a 5% rollout to a quantized LLM variant so we can measure customer-visible regression before committing to a dedicated capacity change.
- As an SRE, I want automatic rollback to prevent regressions from impacting live traffic.
- As a product manager, I want a quick way to compare cost savings and latencies so I can build a business case.

API + UX notes:
- Add small UI microflow in Console: Create Trial -> choose preset -> pick evaluation prompts (or import prompt set) -> schedule -> enable
- API for creating trial should accept a quick eval-set (up to 200 prompts) to run simulated quality checks on the approx variant using historical traces (opt-in).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create trial for an existing route; route-level traffic split works and sampled requests hit approx variant
- Automatic fallback on runtime errors (no customer-visible failures)
- Console shows cost delta and basic success/error metrics; ability to disable trial manually
- Telemetry trace linking sample request IDs to primary/approx outputs for side-by-side inspection

Experiment plan (alpha):
- Q1: small internal alpha with Redwood documentation sites and 3 trusted beta customers (GTM: offering as private alpha)
- Measure: cost per request, latency p95 change, error-rate, manual QA scores on 500 prompt eval set
- Iterate presets for approximation_profile (3 presets: short-context, int8-quantized, small-model)

Open questions / parking lot:
- How to expose model-specific quality regression measures? (simple similarity scores vs. human eval pipeline integration)
- When to charge: trial should not change billing behavior for alpha (but show estimated cost delta). For GA, need billing mapping for per-route pricing.
- Interactions with Dedicated/Private: for Dedicated we need an assignment mechanism to ensure approx variant runs on allowed pools; for Private, trail must respect customer network controls.
- KV cache semantics: do we allow cross-variant KV cache reuse? risk of leakage, need policy.

Implementation notes for eng collaborators:
- Runtime: sampling hook in router layer; small state machine for trial lifecycle (enabled/paused/disabled)
- Console: add trial CRUD + quick eval runner service (re-uses existing eval infra)
- Telemetry: link trial_tag into traces, enrich cost calculation per-token with approximation_profile metadata

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Sync with Mira (eval scope) and Evan (runtime sampling story) — set up 30m
- Draft GitHub PR that adds trial header parsing + sampling stub (rdw/trials)
- Collect 3 candidate eval prompt-sets: onboarding flows, search snippets, code completions

Notes to self:
- Keep presets opinionated; we can always add more later
- Keep it simple for alpha: no multi-route composition, single variant per trial
- Document failure modes clearly in Console (why trial disabled)
